summary: The narrator searches a crumbling complex for a missing person, Halliday, by throwing debris through windows to test for hidden goons, armed sentries, or napalm. A rock thrown into a third-story window sets off a large explosion that blows away the upper floor of a building. Nothing responds, and the narrator concludes the complex's occupants had already left, taking Halliday with them and rigging the building as a trap for anyone who investigated. The passage is an excerpt from a fiction book, Book 6, part 46.
one_line: The narrator probes an abandoned complex by throwing debris through windows, triggering an explosion and concluding the captors have fled with Halliday.
key_facts: The narrator begins a grid search on the other side of the complex, where the buildings looked sturdier.
The narrator pulls hand-sized chunks of metal and concrete from a crumbling tangle of scrap in a stairwell to use as projectiles.
The narrator has a burned hand and wrist, and winces at taking the weight of the debris with them.
The narrator tosses debris through a third-story window, then a second-story window, then a ground-floor window, with no response.
Most windows inside the complex are still glass, and the narrator tracks possible lines of sight and sniper vantage points.
A rock thrown through the third floor of the next building detonates and blows the upper floor apart.
The blast rains brick and concrete onto the street from the height of the third floor.
After the explosion, only one corner of the third-floor walls is still standing, and the rest is rubble of cinder blocks and rebar.
No goons with AKs or napalm respond to the explosion, and nothing moves.
The narrator concludes the occupants had already left, taking Halliday to another location.
The occupants left explosives behind to booby-trap anyone who investigated the abandoned base.
The narrator considers that the occupants probably planned to return but did not expect anyone to follow.

entities.name: Halliday
entities.role: missing person the narrator is searching for; taken from the complex by its former occupants
